sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver, and its effect is strong: risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use climbs, with the largest increase at high utilization.

Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and risk increases with the number of delinquencies on the credit file, with the largest step coming from having none versus at least one.
Income is also among the top three drivers, with an effect of moderate to strong size: higher income generally lowers the risk of default.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, and longer histories generally lower risk.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, since no movement in its curve is resolved.
The effect of utilization does not meaningfully change with credit history length.
The data do not settle whether income and feature_b interact.
The number of recent credit inquiries hardly matters, while the data do not settle whether feature_a matters at all.
